I start tasks, like packing orders or filling out the safety logs, but halfway through, I just lose track. Sometimes I realize I’ve done it wrong or not finished at all. My supervisor’s said I'm disorganized, and I guess I am. It's hard to plan even my daily routine, let alone follow through on anything. I used to be better at managing things, but now it feels like my mind won’t slow down, even though I’m exhausted.

I’m always moving—fidgeting, pacing during breaks, can’t really sit still. Feels like I’m wired, even after eight hours on my feet. But here’s the thing… sometimes I hear someone calling my name when no one’s there. Or I get this strange sense that people at work are talking about me in code, like they’re hiding messages in small talk. I can’t tell if it’s real or if I’m just tired. It’s only popped up in the past few months, maybe? I don’t know when it started exactly. I just know I can’t focus, I’m on edge, and part of me wonders if my head’s playing tricks on me.
D002-D005_h020.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D002-D005_h020.answer: A & C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D002-D005_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling lately—things just feel out of sync. At school, I’ll start explaining a problem on the board and suddenly realize I’ve lost track of where I was mid-lesson. It’s embarrassing. I don’t know if it’s stress or what, but I keep missing deadlines, forgetting to submit grades, and I’ve even left lesson plans at home more than once. Last week I lost my keys again—turned the house upside down. I think I left them in the staff lounge, but I can’t remember.

There are times, especially when I’m tired, that I hear someone calling my name when no one’s there. Sometimes I catch a shadow moving in the corner of my eye, but when I turn, nothing’s there. It doesn’t happen daily, and I know it’s not real—I’m not losing touch with reality or anything—but it’s unnerving. I worry about it, but I can’t focus long enough to unpack why. I used to be organized, but now I’m forgetting doctor appointments, skipping bills. I don’t know if this started recently or if it’s always been this way and I’m just noticing now.

    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D002-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been really struggling lately, especially with keeping up in my classes and managing day-to-day stuff. There are days when I start reading a paper or listening to a lecture, and halfway through, I realize I have no idea what was just said. It’s not that I don’t care—I want to do well—but my mind just drifts, and I lose track. I’ve missed deadlines, forgotten meetings with my advisor, and even lost my student ID twice this semester.  

Sometimes I forget to reply to emails, or I think I paid a bill but didn’t. It’s embarrassing. I used to be organized, but now it feels like I’m constantly chasing after things I’ve dropped.  

Lately, there’s also this weird space in my head. I can’t always tell if certain thoughts are mine or if they’re being placed there. Once, I was alone in my apartment and heard someone say my name—clear as anything—but no one was there. I’ve seen shadows too, just out of the corner of my eye, but when I turn, nothing’s there. I don’t know if it’s stress or lack of sleep, or if I’m just falling apart.  

I don’t remember exactly when the spacing out started—was it before the strange thoughts, or after? I can’t tell anymore.

    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D002-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling a lot lately—just can’t seem to keep up. I’m a taxi driver, so I’m on the road all day, but I’ve been missing pickups, forgetting where I parked, even losing my phone and keys mid-shift. It’s embarrassing. Customers complain, and my dispatch has warned me twice this month about missed rides. I used to be reliable—before the divorce, especially—but now I zone out during conversations, forget errands, and bills pile up until someone chases me.  

Sometimes, I hear a voice muttering my name when no one’s around—usually when I’m tired. It’s not constant, maybe two or three times a week, and I know it’s not real, but it shakes me. I’ve wondered if it’s stress, but then again, I’ve always been scattered. Even in school, I’d start assignments and never finish. Back then, no one called it anything.  

I don’t know when it started—this fog—whether it’s the voices affecting my focus or if I’ve just always been like this and it’s getting worse. Either way, I can’t keep blaming one on the other. They might be together. Or maybe neither is the real problem. I just need to function again.
D002-D005_h023.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Schizophrenia
D002-D005_h023.answer: C & D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D002-D005_h024.question:

At practice, the trainers give us choreography breakdowns, and I try so hard to keep up, but I’ll catch myself realizing I missed half the steps because my mind just… drifted. It’s not that I don’t care—this is my dream—but I’ll start a move and then space out, and by the time I snap back, everyone’s moved on. I’ve lost my dance schedule twice now, and my water bottle, headphones… even my phone, last week, right before a vocal rehearsal. I keep forgetting things—small things, but they pile up. Like whispers when no one’s around, or I’ll feel like someone’s watching me from the corner, but there’s nothing there. It’s not constant—just flickers, really. I can’t tell if it’s stress or if I’m overtired, or… maybe I’m just not cut out for this. The not focusing—it’s been on and off for as long as I remember, but the other stuff? That’s newer. Or maybe I’ve just noticed it more lately. I can’t tell which is causing what anymore.

D002-D005_h025.question:
